raw_response:
I have been farming these plots in Quzhou for 30 years, and I know every corner of my 13.1 mu. My soil is medium loam with decent base fertility, but after three decades of wheat-maize rotation, I pay close attention to nutrient balance. This year, urea is running about 2,800 yuan per ton and 15-15-15 compound fertilizer is around 3,400, so I have trimmed my budget carefully. I keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize double crop because that is my reliable foundation, and I hold 3.1 mu in hybrid Bt cotton. Cotton brings good money when seed cotton hits 7.5 yuan per jin, but it is labor-heavy for picking, so I will not expand beyond what my wife and I can handle during harvest, especially since my son and his wife work off-farm in Shijiazhuang and are only back for busy weekends.

For the winter wheat already in the ground, I learned from last year: I pushed nitrogen to 18 kg per mu and the crop lodged slightly in a late rain. This year I will pull back to 16 kg nitrogen, but I will hold phosphorus at 6 kg and potassium at 6 kg per mu. I need that potassium for stalk strength. I will irrigate three times from my well—green-up water in mid-March, jointing water in early April, and grain filling in mid-May if the sky stays dry. Two spray passes: one herbicide at green-up and one mixed insecticide-fungicide at heading stage. My target is 480 kg per mu; my best plot did 510 last year, but I am being realistic because fertilizer is expensive.

My summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest around June 10th with quick rotary tillage. I plant hybrid seed—never save my own, the hybrid vigor is worth the 60 yuan per mu seed cost. I will put down 16 kg nitrogen per mu, 4 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium. I keep phosphorus lower than wheat because maize scavenges deep and the wheat residue feeds some back. Two well irrigations: one at the seven-leaf stage in July and one at filling in August if the summer monsoon fails. Two sprays: pre-emergence herbicide right after sowing and one ear-stage insecticide when the borers show up. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For the 3.1 mu of cotton, I deep plough in mid-April to break up the hardpan. Cotton is a heavy feeder and I split-feed it: 18 kg nitrogen total per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium, applied as basal, first flower, and peak bloom. I will irrigate three times—establishment, early flowering, and boll filling—and spray four times for aphids, spider mites, and the occasional late bollworm that sneaks past the Bt trait. I am targeting 280 kg per mu of seed cotton. My neighbor cut his fertilizer to save money last year and dropped 40 kg per mu; I would rather spend the extra 150 yuan on nutrients than lose 400 yuan in lint.
